title: Capacity corridors and deterministic autoscale slices — quarterly plan for Dedicated
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Goal: Define and deliver a ‘capacity corridor’ model and deterministic autoscale slices for Dedicated pools to make throughput predictable, reduce expensive overprovisioning, and enable fast-fail canaries for autoscale changes. This work couples policy (corridor bounds, SLAs, hedging rules) with runtime hooks (scale executor, graceful fallbacks) and Console UX (corridor visualization, override controls, canary controls). We will produce a spec, an implementation MVP for a single region/pool type, and a pilot with 3 customers before broad rollout. The initiative balances cost (reservation efficiency), reliability (SLO stability during scale events), and rollout safety (canary/rollback).
acceptance_criteria: Policy spec published with corridor primitives: min, target, max, hedging window, and economic triggers
Runtime autoscale executor implements deterministic slice semantics and exposes metrics for queued scale events
Console UI shows corridor overlays per pool, provides manual overrides, and a canary toggle for new autoscale policies
Pilot completed with 3 internal or customer pools; measured 10–25% reservation efficiency improvements and no >5% regression in 95th p50 latency during pilot
Playbook for canary rollback and emergency capacity increase documented and validated in runbook test

notes_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting — aligned on corridor primitives (min/target/max) and hedging window; agreed to prototype with cpu-type m60 pool first.
2026-03-08: Design review — runtime team prefers deterministic slices over reactive scaling for predictable billing; noted KV cache warmup cost during fast scale-ups as a risk.
2026-03-11: UX sprint started to explore corridor overlays; PM requested ability to annotate corridors with reservation commitments and cost delta.
2026-03-12: Blocker identified — autoscale executor needs a safe fallback when node availability is constrained; ENG-40321 raised to add fallback policy table.
2026-03-13: Decided to instrument two new telemetry tags: corridor_id and hedging_window_ms to enable per-corridor SLO tracking.
decisions: Use deterministic slices (fixed unit increments of capacity) rather than reactive percent-based scaling to keep billing predictable
Pilot will target one GPU family initially (m60) to reduce kernel/quantization variant surface area
Canary behavior: start with traffic-steady rollout (30m), then monitor key signals (queue length, p95 latency, reservation usage) before increasing corridor target
Expose manual override and emergency capacity toggle in Console — no automatic bypass of customer-specified max
risks: KV cache cold-starts may spike tail latency during aggressive scale-ups
Customers with highly bursty usage may be dissatisfied if corridors are too narrow; need override UX to mitigate
Billing complexity: mapping corridor usage to reservation commits may require offline reconciliation in early releases
Region-specific hardware constraints could make uniform corridor defaults inaccurate
